import csv

The current Engine passes the original common-pressure solvent-activity checks
at `{python} identity['temperature_K']` K and `{python} identity['pressure_Pa']` Pa.
For NaCl at `{python} float(first['molality_mol_kg'])` mol/kg water, the osmotic
coefficient is `{python} float(first['osmotic_coefficient'])`. Its absolute
error from the leading Debye relation is
`{python} identity['trace_debye_absolute_error']`, below the original limit
`{python} criteria['trace_absolute']`.

This is numerical verification of the retained fully dissociated aqueous model,
with no new physical validation. The original [qualified replay](results/verification-identity.json)
and [baseline diagnosis](results/diagnosis.csv) remain unchanged. The
[current diagnosis](results/current-main/diagnosis.md) identifies the Engine
changes and the comparisons used to repair the producer.

## Common-pressure definition

The Held packets retain separate hard-chain packing and Debye–Hückel screening
lengths. Their source audit and model limitations are owned by the
[chloride diagnosis](../2026-divalent-chloride-activity/README.md).
Formula-unit molality is per kilogram of water. For $s=\nu mM_w$,

$$
\ln a_w=-\ln(1+s)+\frac{\mu_w^r-\mu_w^{r,\mathrm{pure}}}{RT}
+\ln\frac{\rho_{\mathrm{solution}}}{\rho_{\mathrm{pure}}},\qquad
\Phi=-\frac{\ln a_w}{s}.
$$

The native calculation uses the prescribed common pressure. Subtracting two
separately rounded solvent chemical potentials is retained as a diagnostic;
it does not furnish an independent equality at arbitrary dilution. The
producer checks the ionic and solvent-reference requests at the same composition,
then applies the independent Debye, resolved-change and historical-pressure
checks at their original limits.

## Resolved values and pressure errors

The current replay contains `{python} len(resolved)` resolved comparison rows.
The largest change from the original chloride osmotic values is
`{python} identity['maximum_resolved_change']`, below
`{python} criteria['resolved_absolute']`. The maximum error after accounting
for historical pressure residuals is
`{python} identity['maximum_pressure_corrected_identity_error']`, below
`{python} criteria['pressure_corrected_absolute']`.

The pressure-error identity compares each historical osmotic value with the
historical solution and pure-solvent pressure residuals. Using current root
pressure errors in that identity would compare different density solves.
The [current rows](results/current-main/resolved-comparison.csv) retain original
and current osmotic coefficients, gamma values and densities, as well as the
direct solvent subtraction and removed pressure term. No original row was
replaced. Density and gamma equality checks use the separately rerun current
chloride table at their original limits; the intended ionic-reference correction
is documented in [PR #619](https://github.com/tannerpolley/ePC-SAFT/pull/619).

## Trace availability and limits

```{python}
#| output: asis
print('| Molality, mol/kg | Osmotic coefficient | Reporting outcome | Debye limit |')
print('|---:|---:|---|---:|')
for row in trace:
    print(f"| {row['molality_mol_kg']} | {row['osmotic_coefficient']} | {row['precision']} | {row['debye_limit']} |")
```

Below the retained reporting floor the osmotic quantity remains
`Stop.converged_to_floor`, while ionic activity remains finite. The mixed-solvent
osmotic result remains absent. A numerical reporting floor is not a physical
absence claim, an error bound for arbitrary compositions, or an estimate of
parameter uncertainty.

The [identity](results/current-main/verification-identity.json) retains Engine,
input and script identities and the unchanged criteria. Independent delivered
review remains with the lead. This report has not been promoted for manuscript use.
